state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a favorite video game character who moves forward 3 steps every time they collect a power-up. In this case, the transformation \(y=f(x-3)\) would mean your character is now starting 3 steps ahead from where they used to start. So, the correct translation vector should actually be \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}\) instead.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So if the character is starting 3 steps ahead, that means the graph is actually moving to the right, not up. But why is it a negative 3? I thought the minus sign meant it goes up instead of down. Can you explain that a bit more?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you're playing a treasure hunt game, and the starting point is 3 steps to the left of where you initially thought it was. In this case, the minus sign in \(f(x-3)\) represents moving left, not up. So, the negative 3 in the translation vector is showing the direction the graph is actually moving in.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get it a bit better now! So, when I see \(f(x-3)\), it means the graph moves to the right, which is like starting 3 steps ahead. But I'm still confused about why the minus sign means left instead of up. Does it always work like that with the minus sign?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses confusing analogies that conflate horizontal and vertical directions, provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming the answer is [0, -3] when it should be [3, 0]), and the student remains confused about the fundamental concept throughout, showing no improvement in understanding the horizontal nature of the transformation.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to use real-world analogies (video game character, treasure hunt), these analogies are confusing and actually contradict the mathematical content (claiming the character starts 3 steps ahead but then saying the vector should be negative, and incorrectly stating that minus represents moving left), failing to effectively ground the abstract concept in concrete experience.
